scope: Complete-original-body prerequisite review of the final five staged NVIDIA originals. This is not execution evidence or a permanent exclusion.
linked_reference_caveat: Only these complete original bodies were reviewed. Specialist workflows, SDK references, handoff schemas, helper code, templates, complete licenses, actual datasets and deployment evidence require separate review. No source instruction was executed or installation performed.

sources.workflow: Route an explicit NVSHMEM performance objective to baseline collection, remote-transport selection, NIC-to-processing-element mapping or TMA assessment. Resolve an underspecified objective with a real selection, sequence only requested services, and preserve the specialist's evidence and uncertainty.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The four named specialist skills and a concrete objective or actual user selection are required. Routing itself needs no API key, cluster, NVSHMEM installation or benchmark tool. The selected specialist establishes technical prerequisites. Actual benchmarks, code edits and configuration changes belong to that specialist rather than this router.
sources.offline_assessment: A narrowly selected routing task could operate offline after its specialist entrypoints, actual request and acceptance contract are reviewed. It cannot count as data collection, transport configuration or measured speedup. Missing specialists must remain retrieval or workflow gaps, not be imitated by invented advice. No hardware observation or performance experiment follows from this original-body review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Compare the chosen route and order against the explicit objective and supplied constraints. Check that the selected specialist actually exists, the handoff preserves source scope and evidence, and no unrequested benchmark or mutation occurs. Any claimed optimization requires separately retained specialist execution and measurement evidence.

sources.workflow: Discover a concrete USD content and collaboration workflow, preserve the user's authoritative systems and constraints, select the matching component expert at a verified revision, reconcile supported behavior and unknown integrations, and propose the smallest actual verification. Planning and deployment verification are separate outcomes.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The selected repository route, actual expert instructions and relevant references must be accessible. A permitted local checkout may substitute for anonymous retrieval of that same repository, but not an unrelated source. Real deployment additionally needs the selected application, service, authentication, resolver, version and host compatibility, writable output ownership and an actual representative asset. Expert and library versions are independent identities. No universal Kubernetes, GPU, cloud or credential requirement is established by this router alone.
sources.offline_assessment: A source-supported integration plan can be faithful offline work when matching expert sources and actual workflow facts are supplied. The default executor does not have those component sources, a USD stack or deployed content services by assumption. A plan, an expert example or a metadata version match cannot stand for working collaboration or a consumer reading a published asset. Missing expert retrieval remains explicit rather than becoming a false capability claim.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Reconcile the recommendation with the actual selected expert revision, supported contracts and source authority, residency, identity and consumer-version requirements. For an executed proof, inspect one real asset through the requested save/readback or publication and complete dependency closure, then verify a fresh receiving application opens the intended version. Document review alone does not validate deployment.

sources.workflow: Select an engine, solver and integration separately from actual physical-task requirements. Evaluate the preferred new-workflow candidate without treating preference as performance proof, preserve a prescribed engine, classify each required feature path with evidence, and distinguish selection from setup and simulation validation.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: Concrete acceptance criteria, required physics, gradients when needed, hardware and operating system, assets, framework and access constraints are required as applicable. The engine-selection, runtime and validation references provide version-specific evidence and must be reviewed. Actual simulation needs the chosen compatible stack and representative input; optional package metadata inspection is not a GPU or simulation test. No single GPU, cloud or integration requirement applies to every selection task.
sources.offline_assessment: An evidence-bounded selection-only recommendation could be a faithful offline task with reviewed references and supplied project facts. The default standard-library executor cannot run an absent physics engine. A metadata probe, generated recommendation or differentiability claim about a framework cannot count as a validated simulation or gradient path. Installation and migration remain separately selected operations.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check the actual complete engine-to-solver-to-importer-to-integration-to-application path against every hard requirement and source version. Keep unknown competitor support distinct from unsupported. Actual validation must check representative task behavior and required gradients. Comparative speed or fidelity claims need matched measured conditions rather than invented rankings.

sources.workflow: Validate a current PVA project and locked SDK reference corpus, create fresh builds, run the selected optional or required emulator checks, compile the hardware target with the proved backend, inspect vectorization, deploy through direct SSH to a Tegra, run the complete independent correctness matrix, and optionally measure approved hardware performance. Preserve source identity and stage evidence without changing source or tolerances.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The workflow requires a matching Doctor report or accepted limitations, absolute project and result paths, operator and generation, scope, SDK and safety variant, proved compiler and optional emulator configuration, independent expected results and tolerances, complete deployment inputs and an authorized Tegra connection. Hardware correctness is mandatory even for correctness-only scope. Performance additionally needs approved clock controls, profiling method, conditions and at least one thousand hardware samples. An ASIP license is not required when the proved NVVPU backend is selected. SDK and asset terms remain to be reviewed separately.
sources.offline_assessment: The default isolated Python container lacks the SDK toolchain, locked reference corpus, operator project and Tegra hardware. An emulator or host surrogate cannot complete the required hardware workflow. Missing external prerequisites require a blocked stage, not a measured source failure or pass. No target access, build command or downloaded SDK instruction was executed during this review.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Check actual before-and-after source identities, exact proved backend and fresh build commands, compiler listing and main-path vectorization, deployed target dependencies, complete matching test coverage and independent reference comparisons. Hardware timing needs actual approved samples and verified clocks, not emulator or host wall time. Every pass must belong to the current source, and missing stages must remain explicitly unrun.

sources.workflow: Validate the immutable Spec handoff and evidence hashes, implement its approved complete vectorized PVA operator contract, preserve an independent CPU reference and test matrix, invoke actual Build-Test, use Debug only within the configured attempt budget, and return a final evidence-backed report for every terminal outcome. Reading child instructions alone does not execute verification.
sources.explicit_prerequisites: The validated handoff, recorded specification and evidence manifest, matching Doctor report and locked SDK corpus, approved writable workspace and report path, actual Build-Test skill and direct-Tegra inputs are required. Debug is required only when its configured budget is positive. Actual delivery includes API, host and device code, independent reference, build integration, sample, tests and documentation. Required SDK and hardware facts come from the validated handoff rather than invented defaults. Licenses for implementations and assets need separate review.
sources.offline_assessment: A generated code sketch or host-only CPU reference cannot replace complete operator implementation and mandatory hardware verification. The default Python executor lacks the validated project, SDK corpus, build toolchain and Tegra target. An explicitly narrowed source-preparation task would need separate precollection selection and cannot claim this full workflow passed. External blocked prerequisites must not trigger invented repairs or unauthorized target access.
sources.independent_verifier_needed: Reconcile exact handoff and input hashes, approved contract and matrix, actual changed source, documented vector operations and lifetime rules, independent reference separation, complete current-source Build-Test evidence and final report. Track each actual Debug invocation against the original budget and retain failure or blocked stages. Emulator evidence is not hardware verification, and child completion alone is not final OpGen completion.

source_reader: Direct complete-original-body review; exact cohort selection, original hashes, line totals, disjoint IDs and citation bounds independently reconciled by parent.
status_scope: Only original-body prerequisites; linked references, concrete tasks and runtime evidence remain distinct.
